objective.statement: Understand common directions and signs: pauses, ties, slurs, speed changes and repeats.
successCriteria: I know rall., rit. and accel. change the speed gradually.
I know a pause sign means hold the note longer.
I know da capo means go back to the beginning and fine means the end.

explanation.text: Besides loudness and speed, composers give other directions. Some change the speed during a piece: rallentando (rall.) or ritardando (rit.) means gradually slower; accelerando (accel.) means gradually faster; a tempo means go back to the original speed.

music.textAlternative: A bar of 4/4 with G, A and a minim B with a pause sign above it.

explanation.caption: A pause sign (fermata) over a note: hold it longer than its written length.

explanation.text: A tie joins two notes of the same pitch into one longer sound. A slur is a curved line over different notes and means play them smoothly, joined together.

music.textAlternative: A bar of 4/4 with a slur over the first two notes, G and A.

explanation.caption: A slur over two different notes: play them smoothly.

explanation.text: Da capo (D.C.) means go back to the beginning. Dal segno (D.S.) means go back to the sign. Fine means the end. Ritenuto (riten.) means held back: slower at once. Two small expression words you may meet are dolce (sweetly) and cantabile (in a singing style), and poco means 'a little'. 8va over some notes means play them an octave higher than written. A metronome mark such as M.M. ♩ = 72 gives the exact speed: 72 crotchet beats in a minute.
A tie joins the SAME note; a slur joins DIFFERENT notes. That is how to tell them apart.

music.textAlternative: A bar of 4/4: G and A under a slur, then a minim B with a pause sign.

steps: Look at the curved line over G and A: a slur. They are played smoothly.
Look at the sign over the B: a pause. Hold it longer than its minim length.
A tie would join two notes of the same pitch; here the notes differ, so it is a slur.
demonstration.textAlternative: A bar showing a slur over two notes and a pause sign over the last note.

options.label: play the passage between the marks again

guided.prompt: A curved line joins two different notes. What does it tell the player?

music.textAlternative: A bass-clef stave with two crotchets joined by a curved line.

options.label: play an octave higher than written
play the notes under the curve smoothly
hold the note longer than its written value

hints: Think about whether it is about speed, loudness or how the notes are played.
Staccato is a dot; an accent is a > sign; a pause is a dot under an arc; a curved line over different notes means play smoothly.

feedback.correct: That is what a slur means.

recap: rall./rit. = gradually slower; riten. = held back; accel. = gradually faster; a tempo = back to the speed.
A pause sign: hold the note longer. D.C.: back to the start. D.S.: back to the sign. Fine: the end. 8va: an octave higher.
A tie joins the same note; a slur joins different notes smoothly.

mastery.completion: The lesson is complete when every step has been answered correctly (retries allowed). Only first-attempt, hint-free independent answers count as mastery evidence; guided steps never do.
